event.name: PJM 2026 hot-weather §202(c) emergency
caveats: The authorized window is [verified] from the captured order; whether this facility ran, and for how long inside the window, is [open] — the order is RTO-wide and names no facility. facility_dispatch_confirmed stays False until a facility runtime record lands.

Fleet screen: all 115 permitted units (including P115, rated separately) modeled as separate sources firing together — the reliability-dispatch premise of the Tier-0 cap check. NO monitored background and no other nearby sources are added, which biases the screen LOW: a peak below the NAAQS is a lower bound on the ambient concentration, not a clearance. A peak above it flags the need for a full demonstration, not an automatic violation.

Array layout is a screening assumption: a 11 x 11 grid at 15 m spacing (~150 x 150 m). No record places the stacks; a real layout moves the near-field peak and its location, so where the peak falls is [inference]. Flat terrain and canned met are screening defaults too.
NOx is compared to the NO2 standard as if fully converted (EPA Tier 1), which biases that comparison HIGH; the background omission above biases it LOW. The two do not cancel by any known amount.

Stack geometry is a screening assumption (engine specs not in the record), applied to every unit including any rated separately — the modeled concentration inherits that uncertainty; supersede with manufacturer stack data (SiteFacility.genset_stack_*).

Event-anchored: modeled at the permit LOAD-point rate a real authorized dispatch carries, cited to PJM 2026 hot-weather §202(c) emergency (Order 202-26-33). The authorization window is [verified]; whether this facility ran is [open] (facility_dispatch_confirmed=False) — the concentrations are what such a dispatch would model, not a record that it occurred.
